subject.title: Cron session accumulation can silently exhaust agent context window — no guardrails or warnings

question: Should this umbrella remain open until both isolated cron base-session retention and recurring-job cadence guardrails are resolved, or should maintainers split/close it around narrower canonical work?
rationale: Current source proves the retention gap, but the active related PRs intentionally cover different slices and include compatibility-sensitive choices around live base-row preservation and new cadence policy.

options.title: Keep Umbrella Until Slices Land
options.body: Keep this issue open while reviewing the orphan/base-session retention PR and the cadence guardrail PR, then close or split only after the combined guardrail story is explicit.

options.title: Narrow To Retention Canonical
options.body: Make https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/89666 the retention canonical and track cadence/context warnings separately before closing this umbrella.

options.title: Preserve Base Rows, Add Guardrails Only
options.body: Reject age-pruning live base rows as too risky and pursue only cadence/warning guardrails plus a separate orphan cleanup design.

recommendation.title: Keep Umbrella Until Slices Land
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open while reviewing the orphan/base-session retention PR and the cadence guardrail PR, then close or split only after the combined guardrail story is explicit.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent current-main ownership of the localized cron/session modules makes this the best available routing candidate for the cross-PR behavior decision.
